constraints: The session-replay capture posture is settled: advancedNetworkCapture and consoleCapture in frontend/patches/0009 stay enabled and unchanged. The user reviewed and decided this on 2026-09-15; task 6 pins input masking and fixes comments only
subprocess is imported and called only in launcher/core.py; every other launcher module goes through core.run(), core.capture() or core.popen()

context: Mechanical cleanup sweep following plan feat-merge-ch-otel-demo, which merged ch-otel-demo-eks into this repo and is complete on main at 437 passing tests. Every task here is origin remediation, so this is a SWEEP plan: plan.sweep is true and the deferral ledger is CLOSED, which is deliberate - it stops this cleanup from emitting a ledger that becomes the next sweep's intake. Findings that cannot be applied get one end-of-cycle decision instead. Scope was chosen by the user on 2026-09-15 from the prior cycle's carried items ('everything mechanical'): quality findings q2, q3, q4, q5, q6, q7; security findings sec1 and sec4; and deferrals d1, d9, d15, d18, d19, d23, d30. THREE USER DECISIONS FROM THAT REVIEW BOUND THIS PLAN AND MUST NOT BE REOPENED: (1) the session-replay capture posture stays as-is, which is constraint 1 here and a hard boundary on task 6; (2) the EKS API server stays publicly reachable in the shipped tfvars example (prior-cycle deferral d17, dropped as accepted) - so do not cite 'the cluster is private' as a reason to weaken task 5; (3) three prior-cycle items were left carried UNDISPOSITIONED and are deliberately out of scope here: d3 (the collector's CREATE DATABASE ON otel.* grant, which needs live ClickHouse Cloud validation rather than a static edit), d2 (the profiles pipeline exporting to a disabled firepit, a deployment-design choice) and d16 (the orchestrator-authorised constraint-4 exception for the archived validation transcript). The prior cycle's full evidence is in .claude/plans/feat-merge-ch-otel-demo.json - its security_findings[], quality_findings[] and deferrals[] carry the exact locations and remediations, and its log[] records why each was deferred. READ THE RELEVANT FINDING before implementing a task. One lesson from that cycle is encoded in this plan's wave layout: reserving a shared test file from every task turned a coordination problem into a fake capability gap that cost two evaluator passes, so here each shared file has exactly one owning task and task 8 (which touches nine test files) runs alone in the final wave.

tasks.title: Make the smoke trace-id guard survive python -O
tasks.why: The only non-constant value interpolated into this repo's SQL is guarded by an assert, which optimised mode strips.
tasks.notes: From security finding sec1 (low severity, high confidence). The trace id is read from the storefront's JSON response inside the cluster, so it crosses a trust boundary; with asserts compiled out a misbehaving frontend pod could inject SQL run as the collector's write user, which still holds CREATE DATABASE ON otel.* (deferral d3, left open by user decision). Low severity, one-line fix, and the compounding is why it is worth doing.

acceptance_criteria.text: The full verification command passes
require_trace_id raises unconditionally rather than asserting, mirroring the shape launcher/eks/ops.py already uses for the database name, so the guard survives python -O / PYTHONOPTIMIZE=1
A test proves the guard still refuses a malformed trace id when asserts are disabled - run it under python -O or PYTHONOPTIMIZE=1 rather than asserting the source shape

Audit the rest of scripts/smoke.py for any other assert used as a validation guard on a value that crosses a trust boundary, and report what you find. Fix any you find; the finding named one site but the audit is the deliverable

Note the cluster's WORKLOADS are private but its API server is not - the user accepted that separately (d17), so do not rely on 'the cluster is private' as a reason to weaken this.

Phase 4.5: colored 9 tasks into 4 waves (4/3/1/1). Conflict edges were VERIFIED by grep rather than assumed, and the evidence changed the layout three times. (1) 1-5 is real: launcher/eks/check.py:125 already parses config.COLLECTOR_MANIFEST, so task 5's ac5 would edit the file task 1 owns - separated into waves 1 and 2, which also means task 5 MAY touch check.py freely. (2) 5-7 is real: tests/test_docs.py reads all four READMEs and diffs a Configuration table against .env.example, while task 5 edits README.md, deploy/eks/README.md and possibly .env.example - task 7 moved to wave 3. (3) 2-7 DISSOLVED on inspection: tests/test_cli.py:247 asserts pytest.raises(SystemExit, match='bootstrap first'), and match= is a regex SEARCH, so it survives core.die's 'error: ' prefix and task 2 needs no edit to that file - recorded in task 2's ac notes so an implementer does not 'helpfully' edit it and manufacture the conflict.
